schemaVersion: Ehel Stage 3 Art & Design Placement Exam v1.0
subject: Art & Design
title: Stage 3 Art & Design Starting Check
description: A short, friendly check of what you learned in Grade 2 - printing, colour and weaving, clay, nature and collage, photos and the art corner - so we know where to start and which Grade 2 lessons to look at again.
attemptsAllowed: Unlimited - this check finds your starting point; it is never a fail
feedbackMode: Immediate child-friendly feedback with a starting-point report
_comment: Grade 2's content, asked the Grade 2 way: `pic` and `optionPics` are optional pictures for a young reader (an emoji, `mark:<kind>` for a line drawn by the lesson kit, or `swatch:<hex>`). Review lessons are Grade 2's, and the page links them in ../grade-2-v2/. Built into starting-check.html by ../lesson-kit/build-check.py and checked by ../lesson-kit/check-coverage.py.

ready.label: Ready for Stage 3
ready.message: Brilliant! You remember your printing, weaving, clay and collage like a real artist. Start with Lesson 1 and enjoy Grade 3.

readyWithReview.label: Ready, with a quick look back
readyWithReview.message: You are ready to start Grade 3. Look again at the Grade 2 lessons below first, with a grown-up close by.

notReady.label: Let's look back at Grade 2 first
notReady.message: Let's go back to Grade 2 for a little while. Do the lessons below with a grown-up, then come and try again.

recommendation.label: Grade 2 Art & Design, Lesson 1 with a grown-up

sections.title: Printing, colour and weaving
sections.description: Do you remember what a print is, how a pattern repeats, how black changes a colour, and how weaving works?

sections.title: Clay, nature and collage
sections.description: Do you remember how to join clay, what a sculpture is, what land art is, and when to tear paper?

sections.title: Photos and the art corner
sections.description: Do you remember how to take photos, how to group art, and how to say something kind and true?

questions.correctAnswer: a mark made by pressing and lifting
questions.explanation: Paint the stamp, press it down, lift it up. That is a print.
questions.options: a mark made by pressing and lifting | a mark made with a pencil | a woven thing
questions.question: What is a print?

questions.explanation: The pattern goes circle, star, circle, star, so a circle comes next.
questions.question: Circle, star, circle, star. What comes next?

questions.explanation: Black makes a colour darker. That is a shade.
questions.question: Blue and black make…

questions.explanation: The weft goes across, over and under. The warp is stretched on the loom.
questions.question: The thread that goes across, over and under, is the…

questions.explanation: Scoring makes rough lines that grip, so the join holds.
questions.question: Scratching lines on clay before you join it is called…

questions.explanation: A snowman is made in the round. You can walk all the way round it.
questions.options: a snowman | a painting | a drawing
questions.question: Which one is a sculpture?

questions.explanation: Land art is made outside, from things in nature.
questions.question: Art made outside, from leaves, stones and sticks, is called…

questions.correctAnswer: because a cloud has a soft, fuzzy edge
questions.explanation: A torn edge is soft and fuzzy, like a cloud.
questions.options: because clouds are blue | because a cloud has a soft, fuzzy edge | because tearing is noisy
questions.question: Why tear the paper for a cloud?

questions.explanation: One small thing, very big, is a close-up.
questions.options: far away | a close-up | a flip book
questions.question: A photo of one petal filling the whole picture is…

questions.options: ask them first | take it quickly | share it with everyone
questions.question: What should you do before you take a photo of a person?

questions.explanation: A painted leaf was pressed and lifted, so it was printed.
questions.options: the woven things | the clay things | the printed things
questions.question: A leaf print goes with…

questions.correctAnswer: I love your red, yellow and blue stripes.
questions.explanation: Say something kind that is really in the work: the weaving has stripes.
questions.options: Your clay eyes are beautiful. | I love your red, yellow and blue stripes. | That is messy.
questions.question: The weaver made red, yellow and blue stripes. Which is a kind and true thing to say?
